answer: Reputation-weighted rate limits. Each new identity starts on a thin shale layer: low throughput until its past actions match other identities' outcomes. A bridge rule lets established identities co-sign newcomers, but only up to their own unused quota, so sponsorship is a finite, transferable cost. Overlapping co-signers form a trellis that flags correlated clusters. Attacker cost: buying quota from honest holders plus losing it per failed cluster, scaling linearly with sybil count.
